Sault Ste. Marie Michigan is noted for its Soo Locks,
which allow an average of 10,000 ships per year to
travel between Lake Superior and the lower Great
Lakes. By going through the locks, ships bypass the
rapids of the St. Mary’s River, where the water falls
21 feet from Lake Superior.

SAULT STE. MARIE, Mich. -- The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Detroit District will open the Poe Lock, part of the Soo Locks, in Sault Ste. Marie, Michigan early to all marine traffic at 8 a.m. on March 21st, starting the 2025 Great Lakes shipping season.

"The Soo" is a common nickname for Sault Ste. Marie, Ontario, a city located in Canada on the north shore of the St. Mary's River. It's also the nickname for the Soo Locks, a system of locks that bypass the rapids in the St. Mary's River, connecting Lake Superior to the lower Great Lakes.

Sault St Marie is a city. The Soo Locks are on the Saint Mary River. We vacationed there last year. Neat place, but not a Strait. The Straits are Lake Huron to Lake Michigan and flows under the Mackinac Bridge. It's a major shipping lane between the east coast and Chicago.

Sault St. Marie stays out of it and is safe doing so, because if either of the big powers fucks with them they'll just close off the locks. There's also an implied threat that if things really get out of hand they'll destroy the locks and cut Lake Superior off from the rest of the lakes.

Then there's Sault Ste. Marie and the Soo Locks. Saldy, I don't have a good RIFTSy name for this place, I'm working on it. SSM is an independent city state that controls the Soo locks and access to Lake Superior and the St. Lawrence Seaway.
